settled_groups.title: Evidence provenance and scoped controls
settled_groups.settled_reason: The qualifier identifies the support actually credited to this resource or configuration. Source inspection, observed presence, native failure and missing measurement remain different facts. There is no unresolved editorial question about preserving this scope; completing the missing runtime evidence would be separate work.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: Deleting or globally replacing resource-specific qualifiers with a general assurance would lose which resource/case was actually observed. More precise headings alone do not supply the missing observations.

settled_groups.title: Launch and observation boundaries
settled_groups.settled_reason: The exact observed configuration, observer limitation or accepted census boundary is useful information about the instrument. It remains valid as a scope statement without deciding native facts outside that observation.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: Replacing the observations with a generic inherited-state description would discard the actual control results or the observer's SIGPIPE limitation. Renaming freshness cannot establish a complete authority census.

settled_groups.title: Native/private call boundaries
settled_groups.settled_reason: The account distinguishes PW-owned storage/calls and inspected published implementations from private or installed-library internals. The earlier allocation overclaims and version boundary give this distinction a documented present purpose.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: Saying only that PW calls a native function would erase useful allocation/source findings; calling fixed buffers allocation-free would repeat the overclaim. The boundary remains useful alongside the positive facts.

settled_groups.title: Compiled-profile ownership
settled_groups.settled_reason: The actual rejected lifetime sentence is recorded. No PW free does not decide private apply ownership. The editorial boundary is settled; researching ownership before a future free is a separate implementation question.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: A pointer-retention sentence alone can repeat the allocation-lifetime overclaim. Removing all lifetime discussion would hide a resource constraint relevant to a proposed destruction call.

settled_groups.title: Extension observations and private state
settled_groups.settled_reason: Native outcomes, after-release fresh reads, erasure of owned buffers and unobserved private state have distinct meanings. The accepted limitation and owning contract identify the current basis, including preparation identity versus later opens.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: Renaming S37 to only a worker handle would drop its native-authority/resource subject or move the same private-state qualification elsewhere. Native-call wording alone also cannot turn release success into revocation evidence.

settled_groups.title: Publication and temporal order
settled_groups.settled_reason: The concrete withheld-result effect and the difference between ordered queries and later conditions are useful instrument facts. Keep the independent observation and actual timing consequence; neither needs an inference-origin RCA.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: Replacing the account with completed-slot or query-first vocabulary leaves the same inference available and loses the counterexample or changing-conditions explanation.

settled_groups.title: Review duties and shared verification rules
settled_groups.settled_reason: The source/assertion/execution distinction and call-site review responsibility state the actual workflow. The shared machinery rules govern more than WORKER and remain useful independently of a worker-caption repair.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: Removing the rules after changing WORKER would weaken the stated verification contract or edit other documentation. A caption repair does not supply assertion coverage or a call-site completeness rule.

settled_groups.title: Diagram scope and multiple roles
settled_groups.settled_reason: The legend explains the selected graph and positive multiple-role assignment. These are useful reading facts, not an unresolved claim about a missing worker capability.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: Making the figure exhaustive would require a different account; suppressing multiple roles would discard actual resource roles. No guard-removal repair is needed.

settled_groups.title: Exec outcome layers
settled_groups.settled_reason: Spawn evidence and child/helper outcome are distinct observations in the owning exec contract. The present external basis is identified, so this clarification can stay without a later inference RCA.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: A generic executes-the-target description would obscure which result the worker publishes and make the helper-outcome inference easier.

settled_groups.title: External correlation and pre-apply receipts
settled_groups.settled_reason: The causal and application boundaries define how these useful external/pre-apply observations join the run. Precise source labels do not make the records self-interpreting.
settled_groups.rejected_rewrite: Removing the relation to the run would discard why the observations are present. Renaming association or receipt alone leaves the causal or applied-policy inference available.
